verbalization: Doxorubicin is implicated in the pathogenesis of Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) with the T(8;21)(q22;q22) translocation through a mechanism involving its interaction with leukemia cells. The evidence suggests that Doxorubicin is linked to AML through multiple indirect pathways, with the translocation being a common feature in some cases. Path_3512 and Path_3513 both indicate that Doxorubicin is associated with AML with different translocations, such as T(8;16)(p11;p13) and T(8;21)(q22;q22), and that these leukemias are treated with different drugs. Path_3514 shows that Enasidenib, a drug targeting the AML with T(8;16)(p11;p13) translocation, is also linked to AML with T(8;21)(q22;q22) translocation. This suggests that Doxorubicin may have a role in the development or progression of AML with the T(8;21)(q22;q22) translocation, possibly through a mechanism that involves the drug's antitumor activity in certain subtypes of AML. The integration of these pathways highlights the potential for Doxorubicin to be a candidate for repurposing in the treatment of this specific AML subtype, though further studies are needed to clarify the exact mechanism of action.
